paper.title: Threshold-range scaling of excitable cellular automata

headline: Cyclic CA (Fisch-Gravner-Griffeath 1991): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; n=8 spiral plateau change-fraction=1.00 with colour-return period=8.0=n; n=16 does NOT fixate (final change=1.00) — Moore range-1 threshold-1 n_c is above 16

verdicts.gate: P1 spiral plateau at n=8: mean tail change-fraction > 0.2 (nonzero, non-decaying)
P2 fixation at n=16: change fraction decays to < 0.01
reasons: n=16: max final change-fraction over seeds = 1.0000 (mean tail change 1.0000; need final < 0.01 to count as fixation); the field stays ACTIVE — n=16 is inside the spiral regime for Moore range-1 threshold-1, NOT the fixating regime

verdicts.gate: P3 colour-return period = n at n=8: median return period == 8 (+-1)

extra.framing: CA (disclosed) — synchronous n-colour cyclic cellular automaton on a torus, Moore-8, threshold 1; not agent-stepping
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the cyclic-CA spiral phenomenology (a persistent activity plateau and a colour-return period equal to the number of colours) and honestly flag where the locked spiral->fixation colour count is falsified: for the Moore range-1 threshold-1 rule the critical colour count n_c lies ABOVE 16, so n=16 still spirals rather than fixating

citations: Fisch, R., Gravner, J. & Griffeath, D. (1991). Threshold-range scaling of excitable cellular automata. Statistics and Computing 1(1):23-39. doi:10.1007/BF01890834.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the cyclic-CA spiral phenomenology (activity plateau, colour-return period) and the spiral/fixation colour-count transition
